q: Which cell organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
e: Mitochondria produce energy (ATP) through respiration.

q: The normal body temperature of a healthy human is about:
e: Normal body temperature is about 37 °C (98.6 °F).

q: Deficiency of Vitamin D causes:
e: Lack of Vitamin D weakens bones and causes rickets in children.

q: Scurvy is caused by the deficiency of:
e: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, with bleeding gums.

q: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
e: O negative red cells lack A, B and Rh antigens, so they can be given to most people.

q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
e: The human heart has two atria and two ventricles.

q: Photosynthesis takes place in which cell organelle?
e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps sunlight for photosynthesis.

q: Malaria is caused by:
e: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium and spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes.

q: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
e: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones; a newborn has about 300.

q: Insulin is produced by which organ?
e: Beta cells in the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas make insulin.

q: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
e: The liver is the largest gland in the human body.

q: Deficiency of iodine in the diet causes:
e: Iodine is needed for thyroid hormone; its lack enlarges the thyroid (goitre).

q: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
e: The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone; the femur is the longest.

q: Haemoglobin contains which metal?
e: Iron in haemoglobin binds oxygen in red blood cells.

q: What is the structural and functional unit of the kidney?
e: Each kidney has about a million nephrons that filter blood.

q: The ABO blood group system was discovered by:
e: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood groups in 1901.

q: Penicillin was discovered by:
e: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from Penicillium mould in 1928.

q: Typhoid is caused by a:
e: Typhoid is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi.

q: Which of these is a viral disease?
e: Measles is caused by a virus; TB, cholera and typhoid are bacterial diseases.

q: Which part is called the natural 'pacemaker' of the heart?
e: The SA node starts each heartbeat.

q: The average lifespan of human red blood cells is about:
e: RBCs live about 120 days and are then destroyed mainly in the spleen and liver.

q: Gregor Mendel, the father of genetics, did his experiments on:
e: Mendel studied inheritance in the garden pea (Pisum sativum).

q: Which plant hormone helps in the ripening of fruits?
e: Ethylene is a gaseous hormone that speeds up fruit ripening.

q: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human body (somatic) cell?
e: Human somatic cells have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs); gametes have 23.

q: The enzyme present in human saliva is:
e: Salivary amylase starts the digestion of starch in the mouth.

q: Which cell organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
e: Ribosomes join amino acids to make proteins.

q: The Rh factor in blood is named after:
e: The Rh antigen was first found in Rhesus monkeys.

q: Which part of the brain maintains balance and coordinates voluntary movements?
e: The cerebellum controls posture, balance and fine movement.

q: The study of fungi is called:
e: Mycology is the study of fungi; phycology is the study of algae.

q: The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) takes place in the:
e: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, while the Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
